question: What does drug over-prescription mean in clinical practice?

options.A: Storing too many pharmaceutical products in the hospital pharmacy
options.B: Giving medicines that are unnecessary or in too high a dose
options.C: Ordering only herbal remedies instead of orthodox drugs
options.D: Failing to give any medication to a critically ill patient

explanation: Over-prescription happens when patients receive drugs they do not need or take excessive quantities that can harm them. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of the National Drug Policy in Nigeria?

options.A: To ensure medicines are safe, effective, and properly used
options.B: To give nurses the sole legal power to write prescriptions
options.C: To make every single medication free for all citizens
options.D: To stop all foreign pharmaceutical companies from importing drugs

explanation: The policy sets standards to protect the public by regulating drug quality, distribution, and rational use. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why do some patients pressure doctors to write unnecessary prescriptions?

options.A: They believe getting a drug means they received good care
options.B: They are legally required to buy three drugs per visit
options.C: They prefer paying more money for hospital visits
options.D: They want to study pharmacology at the university

explanation: Many patients feel unsatisfied with a consultation unless they walk away with physical items like tablets or syrups. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h2)

question: How can time pressure in a busy clinic contribute to over-prescription?

options.A: Doctors have more time to carefully review every single medical chart
options.B: Clinicians may quickly write prescriptions to end consultations faster
options.C: Nurses take over all prescribing duties to reduce doctor workload
options.D: Patients automatically leave the clinic without asking for drugs

explanation: When clinics are overcrowded, writing a prescription takes less time than explaining why a drug is not needed. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is polypharmacy generally defined as?

options.A: Stopping all medications abruptly without advice
options.B: Taking five or more medications concurrently
options.C: Injecting a single drug twice a day
options.D: Using only traditional herbs for chronic illnesses

explanation: Polypharmacy refers to the use of multiple drugs at the same time, commonly set at a threshold of five or more. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h3)

question: What happens during a prescribing cascade?

options.A: The pharmacy runs out of basic supplies and substitutes vitamins
options.B: A drug side effect is mistaken for a new illness and treated with another drug
options.C: All medications are washed out of the patient's system at once
options.D: A nurse stops all prescriptions due to a sudden power outage

explanation: The prescribing cascade creates a dangerous cycle where side effects lead to more prescriptions instead of drug discontinuation. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h3)

question: What major public health threat is directly worsened by the over-prescription of antibiotics?
explanation: Unnecessary antibiotic use teaches bacteria how to survive drug treatments, creating resistant strains that are hard to cure. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h4)

question: An elderly patient taking many unnecessary drugs is most at risk for which problem?

options.A: Rapid increase in daily physical activity
options.C: Severe adverse drug reactions and toxicity
options.D: Complete immunity to all common infections

explanation: Older adults process drugs more slowly, making them highly vulnerable to side effects and dangerous drug interactions. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is a key action during a nursing medication review?

options.A: Telling the patient to stop taking all prescribed treatments
options.B: Changing the hospital's drug supply company without approval
options.C: Comparing prescribed drugs against the patient's current diagnoses
options.D: Ordering new laboratory equipment from foreign manufacturers

explanation: A proper review ensures every medication matches a genuine, active medical need rather than an outdated or unverified condition. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is it important to ask patients about herbal supplements during a medication review?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost of traditional medicines
options.B: To replace all hospital pharmacies with local herb shops
options.C: To report illegal herbal sellers to the local police department
options.D: To check for hidden interactions with prescribed orthodox drugs

explanation: Herbal products can interact strongly with prescription medications, altering their effects or increasing toxicity. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is one effective nursing action during a multidisciplinary ward round?

options.A: Writing new drug orders without consulting the attending doctor
options.B: Hiding the prescription chart from the medical team
options.C: Discharging all patients who take more than two tablets daily
options.D: Questioning unnecessary prescriptions and suggesting alternatives

explanation: Nurses act as safety advocates by speaking up when a medication order appears unsafe or clinically unjustified. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h6)

question: How does educating a patient help reduce inappropriate drug use?

options.A: It prevents them from ever visiting a hospital clinic again
options.B: It helps them understand why they do not need certain medicines
options.C: It forces pharmaceutical companies to lower medication prices
options.D: It gives them the legal right to prescribe drugs to neighbors

explanation: When patients understand the risks of unnecessary drugs, they are less likely to demand them from clinicians. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which Nigerian agency is heavily involved in regulating drug safety and distribution?
explanation: NAFDAC is the primary federal agency responsible for regulating and controlling the manufacture, importation, and sale of drugs in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h7)

question: What is the main goal of hospital antibiotic stewardship programs?

options.A: To encourage patients to take antibiotics for common colds
options.B: To ban all antibiotics from being stored in the country
options.C: To make expensive antibiotics available for free to staff
options.D: To promote the correct, rational use of antimicrobial drugs

explanation: Stewardship programs monitor and guide prescribing practices to prevent misuse and slow down antimicrobial resistance. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h7)
